thread:
anna: Quick check — we're choosing between a thin edge JSON gateway (browser-friendly) that forwards to internal gRPC services, vs a shared gateway that does full proto translation and enforces quotas. Thoughts?

mike: My gut says thin edge + sidecar for translation when needed. Keeps edge simple and lets service teams own contract.

sam: +1 for simplicity at the edge but worried about cross-tenant quota enforcement. If translation is per-sidecar we need a central quota decision point.
julia: What does the console UX look like for teams to see quota usage and routing? We need per-route visibility even if translation lives in sidecars.

ben: If we go with shared gateway, we can attach per-route weights and failover policies centrally (canary, fallback to smaller models). But cost attribution becomes harder unless we propagate trace/route id.

anna: Ops-bot: can you remind folks of the telemetry sampling limits we have?

ops-bot: Telemetry policy: default traces 1/min per service, metrics granularity 30s, high-sampling opt-in for canary routes. See https://console.internal/telemetry/policies

mike: If sidecars emit a route_id header to tracing and metrics, console can stitch usage even with decentralized translation. That header needs to be authenticated though.

sam: Could we have a lightweight control plane endpoint that sidecars call for quota checks/routing decisions? Keeps enforcement central, translation local.  Example flow:
```
client -> edge (json) -> sidecar translates -> ctrlplane/check -> backend (grpc)
```

julia: That would let the console show "per-route" dashboards without forcing every payload through a heavy gateway. We can also show rollout stage (canary/95pct) per route.

ben: Downsides: added hop adds ~8-15ms p50 if ctrlplane is external. We can cache decisions for 1s to shave latency. Also need to think about burst quotas.

anna: Performance numbers matter. Can we prototype: sidecar + ctrlplane-check with 1s cache vs shared-gateway baseline and measure p50/p95 and 99 for small text requests?

mike: I'll spin up a small lab today. Target scenarios: browser-origin requests (CORS), internal service-to-service (gRPC) and fallback paths.

sam: Also include quota saturation test (200 tenants hitting limit) — check CPU on control plane.

julia: UX asks: expose a "routing inspector" in console that shows live route decision, last 5 checks, and active canary fraction. Also surface cost-per-token estimates if route uses a bulky variant.

ben: For contract format: prefer proto for service-to-service, but keep edge JSON shape stable. Provide a small schema mapping tool that generates lightweight stubs for clients.

anna: Agreed. Next steps: Mike prototype, Sam load test ctrlplane, Julia mock console widgets, Ben draft contract mapping tool. We'll reconvene EOD Friday. :thumbsup:

mike: ack — ping me in this thread if you want to join the lab.

julia: I'll make a quick Figma for the routing inspector.

sam: Adding a checklist to the RFC PR now.

anna: Thanks all — trying to avoid a heavy gateway while keeping centralized policy and observability.
